concept.concept_description: The EML single operator f(x) = e^a * log(b*x + c) is a contraction mapping for suitable parameter ranges. Conjecture: For all a, b, c in R with a > 0 and b, c chosen so that the function maps a closed interval to itself, the iteration x_{n+1} = e^a * log(b*x_n + c) converges to a unique fixed point x* at a rate O(rho^n) where rho = |f'(x*)|. Test: prove convergence for the specific case a in (0,1), b=1, c in (0,1) and compute the fixed point explicitly as a series. Impact: establishes EML as having well-defined dynamical behavior, enabling EML-based iterative algorithms with certified convergence.

relation to OEIS A080170 `D(k) = gcd_{2 ≤ q ≤ k+1} C(q·k, k)`.

`F(k) = D(k)` for every `k ≥ 3`, and the two differ only at `k = 2`.

The key insight is that the only term dropped when truncating `Icc 2 (k+1)` to
`Icc 2 k` is `q = k + 1`, and Kummer's carry count shows this term's `p`-adic
valuation is never the strict minimiser for any prime `p ∣ k+1` once `k ≥ 3`, so

(`not_pSq_dvd_central`); the remaining step is a uniform "the last term is
dominated" lemma, which is within reach of the existing Kummer toolkit.

`F(k) = 1` if and only if the largest exact prime-power component `P` of `k + 1`
satisfies `P² < k + 1` (equivalently `(k+1)/P > P`).

The key insight is that the mission's "`k` is a prime power" predicate is an
off-by-one error: every divisibility argument is driven by the base-`p`
representation of `k + 1`, not of `k`, because `C(q·k, k)` carries are governed
by `q·k = q(k+1) - q`. Why now? This cycle already proves the `⇐`-nontriviality
half (`F_ne_one_of_succ_primePow`) and the exact prime-fibre valuation; the open
half is the constructive `⇒` (build, for each prime `p ∣ k+1` with `p^{v} ≤ √(k+1)`,
a witness `q` with a single carry), the same construction needed for A080170.

## Conjecture 3 — exact `p`-adic valuation formula off the prime fibre

For `k + 1 = p^a · m` with `p ∤ m` and `1 ≤ a`, the exponent of `p` in `F(k)` is
`a - ⌊log_p m⌋` (truncated at `0`).

The key insight is that the gcd's `p`-part is the *minimum over `q`* of the
carry count `v_p(C(q·k,k))`, and that minimum is attained by the `q` that aligns
the top nonzero digit of `m` with a borrow, costing exactly `⌊log_p m⌋` carries
out of the available `a`. Why now? The prime-fibre case `m = 1` is settled here
(`factorization_F_pred`), giving the base case `a - 0 = a` of an induction on the
number of nonzero base-`p` digits of `m`.

There are infinitely many `k` with `F(k) ≠ 1` and `k` not a prime power, and
infinitely many `k` with `F(k) = 1` and `k` a prime power.

The key insight is Dirichlet's theorem: primes `p ≡ 1 (mod 6)` give `k = p - 1`

concept.concept_description: In the h=1 specialization of additive strong blocking sets, i.e. ordinary strong blocking sets in PG(2,2), a finite set S of projective points is strong blocking if and only if it contains at least 6 of the 7 points. concept.lean_guess: Represent points of PG(2,2) as 1-dimensional submodules of V = (ZMod 2)^3 and lines as 2-dimensional submodules. In the Fano plane every line has exactly 3 points and any two distinct points determine a unique line. A set S is strong blocking exactly when every line contains at least two points of S. If S is strong blocking, its complement cannot contain two points, since those two points would determine a line meeting S in only one point; hence |S| ≥ 6. Conversely, if |S| ≥ 6, every line misses at most one point, so it contains at least two points of S and therefore its intersection with S spans the line.
